clue.text: Party 'amending 'bill out of time

indicators.note: amending a bill means altering it, so these letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A political party is changing a bill that has run out of parliamentary time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amending' rearranges BILL together with ERA (time); 'out of' just says what the letters are made from.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberals are a British political party, so the name stands for a party.

clue.text: Do its northern inhabitants-run round in circles?.

definitions.text: Do its northern inhabitants-run round in circles?

parts.words: Do its northern inhabitants-run round in circles?
parts.note: a run round a circuit is a lap, so a country of people who lap would be named so; also the Arctic region of the Sami

explanation.surface: Do people in the far north go round in circles?
explanation.walkthrough: The region's people were called Lapps; a lap is a circuit, hence the joke of people running round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic region of northern Scandinavia and Finland, home of the Sami.

clue.text: Covering the dormitory beanfeast?

parts.note: a dormitory is filled with places to sleep, each a cot
a spread is a lavish meal, as a beanfeast is

explanation.surface: Is a midnight feast in the dormitory being hidden?
explanation.walkthrough: A beanfeast is British slang for a celebratory meal; the picture is a midnight feast laid out on a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative cover laid over a bed is a covering.

clue.text: Non-carbon coloured' chalk material

indicators.note: non means without, so the letter for carbon is dropped

parts.note: a crayon is a stick of coloured chalk or wax
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A coloured chalk containing no carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-carbon' removes C from CRAYON.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial silk fabric, a cloth made from cellulose.

clue.text: No doubt his deeds have been witnessed

definitions.text: No doubt his deeds have been witnessed

parts.words: No doubt his deeds have been witnessed
parts.note: sounds like a man whose actions had onlookers, but means title deeds to property, signed before witnesses

explanation.surface: Without question, people have seen what he did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deeds' looks like actions; they are legal documents proving ownership of property.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who holds property, whose title deeds were signed before witnesses.

clue.text: How the Thunderer spoke having thus seen through deception?

definitions.meaning: a thunder god's voice gave a low rolling roar; 'the Thunderer' is also the nickname of The Times itself
in British slang, to have someone's trick found out

explanation.surface: A thunderous voice declares that a fraud has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Thunderer' is both Jove and the old nickname of The Times newspaper; 'having thus' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder makes a low growling roll, and in British slang a fraud that is found out has been exposed in exactly this word.

clue.text: Real trouble for her father

parts.note: the letters of real, rearranged, spell the Shakespeare king whose cruel daughter caused him real trouble

explanation.surface: She was a genuine headache for her dad.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, one of his two cruel daughters; 'Real' in trouble gives LEAR, her father.
explanation.definitionFit: One of King Lear's ungrateful daughters in Shakespeare, who turned against her father.

clue.text: Memento or maybe something to mark the time

indicators.note: maybe suggests these letters could be another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: A keepsake might help someone keep track of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the nine letters of 'Memento or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticking device musicians use to keep a steady beat.

clue.text: Permission not to interfere

explanation.surface: Someone is given approval provided they keep out of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent or authorised absence, and also to let things be without meddling.

clue.text: Some padres denigrate China

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few priests run down the country of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is porcelain, named after the German city where it is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain from Meissen near the German city of that name is a kind of china.

clue.text: Play ends with cast in a rage

indicators.note: in puts the next piece inside the letters already chosen
the ends of the word play are its first and last letters

parts.note: to cast up a column of figures is to add them

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a temper over the casting of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' here is the old bookkeeping sense, to cast up a column of figures; 'a rage' must take the article so it can stand for the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British informal speech for a temper tantrum, a fit of anger.

clue.text: Something moving near might disturb our sleep

definitions.text: Something moving near might disturb our sleep

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of these two words are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A thing creeping close at night could wake us up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the nine letters of 'near might'; the whole clue also describes a bad dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream that frightens a sleeper is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Instrument for blowing up mountains

parts.note: sounds like explosives for demolishing peaks, but means a long wooden horn blown high up in the Alps

explanation.surface: A device for demolishing mountains with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' suggests explosives; read it as blowing a horn up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: This long Alpine wind instrument is played by herdsmen high in the mountains.

clue.text: Mountain maid hands out request 'to palmist

definitions.meaning: a nymph of the hills in Greek myth
a client holding out their hands might say 'Oh, read!' to a fortune-teller

explanation.surface: A girl from the hills holds out her palms to have her fortune told.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is playful: the five letters split as O, READ, an exclamation a client might make while offering their palms.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology these nymphs lived in mountains, so the word names a mountain nymph.

clue.text: Stayed newly wed with a junior officer

indicators.note: newly means made afresh, so the letters of wed are put in a new order

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a junior officer

explanation.surface: A newly married person spent time with a lieutenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges WED to give DEW, followed by LT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived or remained somewhere is the past tense of abide or reside.

clue.text: "Now spurs the lated apace To. gain the timely inn" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: "Now spurs the lated apace To. gain the timely inn" (Macbeth)

parts.words: "Now spurs the lated apace To. gain the timely inn" (Macbeth)
parts.note: the quotation from Macbeth has a word missing after lated, the one who spurs on to reach the inn

explanation.surface: A line from Macbeth about someone hurrying to reach an inn by nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the word missing from the First Murderer's line in Macbeth, Act 3: a belated wayfarer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a journey, the belated wayfarer of Shakespeare's line.

clue.text: Went on in a novel way referring to philosopher

indicators.note: doing something in a novel way means arranging these letters afresh

explanation.surface: Someone talked at length about an original thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a novel way' rearranges the nine letters of 'Went on in a'; Isaac Newton was described in his day as a natural philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective formed from the name of the natural philosopher who gave us the laws of motion.

clue.text: Small -creature to grow in body

parts.note: to wax is to grow, as the moon does
a sect is a body of believers

explanation.surface: A tiny creature grows inside a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' looks like a physical body; it is a religious group, a sect.
explanation.definitionFit: A small scale bug that secretes wax, such as the Chinese white-wax bug.

clue.text: Average position of a buffer state

definitions.meaning: middling, neither one thing nor the other
a neutral country sits in the middle of two rival powers

explanation.surface: A neutral country typically sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or intermediate, and also the place of a neutral country lying in the middle of two powers.

clue.text: Press and TV trade secrets, say, with lady 17?

parts.note: newspapers and television together are the media

indicators.note: say means the word that follows is to be heard as spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the tricks of the trade are its secrets

explanation.surface: The press and TV are spilling professional secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the down answer meaning a go-between; the answer is a woman who mediates. 'say' turns TRICKS into the sound-alike TRIX.
explanation.definitionFit: A female mediator, the feminine form of a word for a go-between or intercessor.

clue.text: Silent about skirt riding up — least one can do

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum

indicators.note: in a down clue riding up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: Someone keeps quiet about their skirt riding up, the least they can do.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'riding up' reads the skirt word from the bottom upwards; 'about' wraps the word for silent round that.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest acceptable amount, the lowest possible effort.

clue.text: Push for this room to work in

definitions.meaning: to jostle someone aside with a bent arm
space enough to move freely is named after the joint of the arm

explanation.surface: Someone shoves to make space for working.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove with the arm joint, and the same word joined to 'room' means space to move freely.

clue.text: House' or Castle?

definitions.meaning: the British royal family's dynastic name since 1917
the royal castle in Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: Is it a home or a fortress?
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are royal: the name of the British royal house and its castle in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the British royal dynasty and of the monarch's Berkshire fortress.

clue.text: Boldness may cause sensation.

definitions.meaning: a fibre carrying feeling from the body to the brain

explanation.surface: A daring act can create a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensation' looks like a stir or scandal, but means physical feeling, which a fibre of the body carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage or cheek is one sense; the other is a fibre carrying feeling to the brain.

clue.text: Frenchman took some stick in "art circles

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A Frenchman was criticised heavily in the art world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took some stick' suggests criticism; 'in art circles' points to the sculptor Auguste Rodin and is part of the scene rather than the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: A detective in Becky's academy?

definitions.meaning: an agent of the famous American private detective agency
in Thackeray's Vanity Fair, Becky Sharp is educated at Miss ___'s academy for young ladies

explanation.surface: Is there a sleuth at the school a girl called Becky attends?
explanation.walkthrough: Becky is Becky Sharp, heroine of Thackeray's novel Vanity Fair, who goes to a girls' school in Chiswick run by a lady of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of an American detective agency and of the schoolmistress in Vanity Fair.

clue.text: Put : on a coat of many "colours?

definitions.text: Put : on a coat of many "colours?

parts.words: Put : on a coat of many "colours?
parts.note: suggests Joseph's robe, but means applying a coat of a coloured finish to a surface

explanation.surface: Wear Joseph's famous technicolour coat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat of many colours' recalls Joseph's robe in Genesis; here a coat is a layer of colour applied with a brush.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate a surface by brushing on a coloured coating.

clue.text: One no credit to strikers

parts.note: in cricket, a run such as a wide or bye that is not credited to the batsman on strike

explanation.surface: Someone who does nothing to help workers on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikers' looks like workers on strike; in cricket the striker is the batsman facing the bowling, and some runs are scored without being credited to him.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a run added to the total but not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide.

clue.text: Nominally she takes the cake

parts.note: a girl's name which is also the name of a small French sponge cake, so she takes the cake in name

explanation.surface: In name only, she wins the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the cake' sounds like winning; 'Nominally' says her name is the name of a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name that is also a small shell-shaped French sponge, as in Proust.

clue.text: Hardy lass seen around river lock'

indicators.note: seen around means the first piece is wrapped round the next one

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy's heroine is spotted near a lock on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' looks like a canal lock beside the river; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl or long strand of hair is a lock.

clue.text: Place of call for the faithful

definitions.text: Place of call for the faithful

parts.words: Place of call for the faithful
parts.note: not a place the faithful visit, but the tower from which they are called to prayer

explanation.surface: A spot that devout people drop in at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place of call' suggests a stop on a journey; here it is where the call to prayer is given.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall tower of a mosque, from which the muezzin calls Muslims to prayer.

clue.text: Score may reflect quality of his groundwork

definitions.text: Score may reflect quality of his groundwork

parts.words: Score may reflect quality of his groundwork
parts.note: the score of a match shows how well a coach drilled the team on the training ground

explanation.surface: A tally might show how well someone did the spadework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groundwork' is preparation done on the practice ground by a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach who prepares players or racehorses, whose results show how good the preparation was.
